steps.say: Hold W at a brick pillar in a video world model.

steps.caption: Raw model on the left, NoPeWorld on the right
steps.say: The raw model walks straight through. The same input with NoPeWorld stops at the bricks.

scenes.headline: Walls are solid, and the model already knows it
scenes.sub: NoPeWorld, from PolyU's Learning and Generation Lab
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kerb. These models have no physics engine, so nothing says no. NoPeWorld adds the no, and leaves the generator alone.

scenes.title: One decision, before the chunk is drawn

params.slide: dashed: what a game engine does
params.pick: run the safe one closest to it

steps.say: From above. The camera walks at an angled wall, and the raw model's path runs right through it.

steps.term: Candidates: the input, a stop, shorter steps, turns
steps.say: So at every chunk, score 34 candidate motions. Sweep a disc along each. Red would touch the wall, green keeps its margin.
A game engine would slide along the wall. Pick the green one closest to that.
And the camera slides, instead of passing through.

scenes.title: Where the safety score comes from

steps.say: There is no map at test time, and the generator stays frozen.
But its hidden states carry the geometry, so the head reads a few middle and deep blocks.

steps.term: Head: under 2M parameters per world model
steps.say: Each candidate is added to every token, and two cross-attention blocks read the grid.
Out comes a safety and an intent score per candidate. An unsafe input gets swapped.

scenes.title: The same head, reading different inputs
scenes.note: AUC for an unsafe input, the paper's Table S11
scenes.say: Why the DiT? On decoded pixels the same head is close to a coin flip. On DiT states it separates safe from unsafe almost perfectly.

states.term: NoPeBench: every route drives into an obstacle
states.say: NoPeBench places each generated video on the true map. The raw model goes through, or erases, the obstacle on 89 routes of 100.
With the head in collision mode, 7 are left. Most of the rest are stops, and only 13 slides.

scenes.title: Against a depth guard that just halts

left.title: External depth
items: Decode every chunk, run Depth Anything 3
left.say: A depth guard that halts on every chunk has fewer violations on average, about ten percent.

right.title: NoPeWorld
items: Slides, and costs 0.09 s a decision
right.say: NoPeWorld lands at sixteen, but it slides instead of freezing, and costs almost nothing.

scenes.text: The generator already knows where its walls are. A small head turns that into a choice of motion.
scenes.mark: already knows where its walls are
scenes.say: The model already knows where its walls are. A tiny head turns that into the motion you get.

recap: Slides where a depth guard freezes
scenes.say: Thirty-four candidates, read from the DiT, and a camera that stops at the wall. Thanks for watching!
